answer: One practical defense is a bonded identity deposit: every new agent must lock a modest stake, worth perhaps a handful of copper coins, for ninety days before its votes or attestations count. An honest user barely notices, but an attacker spinning up a nebula of ten thousand fake agents must freeze ten thousand deposits, and any caught colluding are slashed. Like water seeping through shale, influence accrues slowly, so flooding the network becomes costly instead of free.
